title: Computer Networking I

prerequisites.expression: CS 2200 with a minimum grade of C or ECE 3057 with a minimum grade of C or ECE 3058 with a minimum grade of C

requirements_fulfilled: Distributed System & Software Design and Systems & Architecture Thread — Computer Networking I (1 class in CS 3251)
description: Introduction to problems in computer networking, including error recovery, medium access, routing, flow control, and transport. Emphasis on current best practice. Includes programming of networked applications.
skills_developed: Understand how computer networks are designed and how they operate.
Use network measurement and troubleshooting tools.
Solve mathematical problems about network performance.
Recognize design challenges in wide-area, datacenter, wireless, and cellular networks.
Build networked applications and network protocols.
topics_covered: computer networking concepts, protocols, and technologies
the current Internet as a case study
exam_structure: 3 in-person pen-and-paper exams: an in-class midterm (25%), an in-class programming quiz (12%), and a cumulative final during finals period (32%). One A4 sheet is allowed on the midterm, one on the programming quiz, and two on the final. No internet or AI on exams.
grading_breakdown: 3 homework assignments at 7% each (21%), 1 programming assignment 10%, in-class midterm 25%, in-class programming quiz 12%, cumulative final 32%. Scale: A>=90, 90>B>=80, 80>C>=70, 70>D>=60, 60>F. No curve stated. Homework is graded on completion and good-faith effort, not on correctness of individual answers.
assignment_load: 3 homework assignments and 1 sockets programming assignment, submitted on Canvas. Required textbook: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, Kurose and Ross, 9th edition. Late policy: 1-hour grace period, 10% penalty under 24 hours, 20% penalty from 24 to 48 hours, not accepted after 48 hours.

has_lab.note: Syllabus lists homework, one programming assignment, and in-person exams. No lab component is stated.

average_gpa.note: Aggregate across sections, not per instructor.

notable_features: Exams are 69% of the grade (midterm, programming quiz, and cumulative final), so the tag is exam-heavy. Homework is only 21% and is not graded for correctness. Sections A and B share TAs but can differ in topic order and grading; students must follow the section they are registered in. Lectures are in person and are not livestreamed.
source: GT Course Information popup; Fall 2026 section A syllabus

title: Processor Design

prerequisites.expression: (CS 2200 with a minimum grade of C or ECE 3057 with a minimum grade of C or ECE 3058 with a minimum grade of C) and ECE 2031 with a minimum grade of C

requirements_fulfilled: Distributed System & Software Design and Systems & Architecture Thread — Comp Structures: Hardware/Software Codesign of a Processor (1 class in CS 3220)
description: Introduces traditional processor architectures and dedicated AI accelerator architectures through lectures and hands-on laboratory work. Follows CS 2200. Emphasizes implementing basic processor modules in Verilog, including pipeline design, operation parallelism, and on-chip communication. Topics include Verilog, FPGA programming, pipeline design, parallel architecture, NoC design, RISC-V processors, AI accelerators, Xilinx FPGA tools, and Pynq boards. Catalog description: principles in pipelined processor design, with emphasis on a close interaction between code generation and architecture.
skills_developed: Understand pipelining, operation parallelism, on-chip communication, NoC design, and RISC-V-based systems.
Design and implement basic hardware modules using Verilog, FPGA workflows, Xilinx tools, and Pynq boards.
Apply concepts from traditional processors and dedicated AI accelerators in laboratory assignments.
Debug, test, and iterate on individual hardware designs.
exam_structure: No midterm or final exam is stated. An entrance exam is 3% bonus credit.
grading_breakdown: Participation, short assignments, and attendance 20%. Lab assignments 80%. Entrance exam 3% bonus. Scale: A 90–100, B 80–89, C 70–79, D 60–69, F below 60. No curve stated. Late submissions are not accepted without prior approval.
assignment_load: Lab assignments are 80% of the grade and are individual. Lecture notes are the course materials. Optional reference: Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach. Three or more absences or excessive lateness can negatively affect the final grade.

has_lab.note: Hands-on laboratory work is 80% of the grade, using Verilog, Xilinx FPGA tools, and Pynq boards.

average_gpa.note: Aggregate across sections, not per instructor.

exam_structure: 1 take-home final exam worth 10%, completed individually during a stated exam week. It covers videos, readings, activities, and project material.
grading_breakdown: Class participation 40% (readings, discussions, in-class exercises, graded quizzes, and 1 graded group exercise). Project deliverables 50% in the summary table. The listed project pieces are proposal and teaser video 10%, halftime update 10%, final presentation and demo 10%, and final report 15%, which sum to 45%, not 50%. Exam 10%. Scale: 90–100% A, 80–89% B, 70–79% C, 60–69% D, below 60% not passing. No curve stated.
assignment_load: One semester-long group project in teams of at least four, with a team contract, proposal and teaser video, halftime update, demo, and report. About 10 topic blocks with practical exercises, often in teams, after prerecorded videos and readings. CITI IRB training is required before project work. A hardware starter kit is about $45 if the student does not already have similar parts. Textbook used: Ubiquitous Computing Fundamentals, John Krumm, 1st edition, with more weight on scientific articles than on that book.

has_lab.note: No separate lab section is stated. In-class prototyping exercises use a microcontroller and sensor kit.

average_gpa.note: Aggregate across sections, not per instructor.

notable_features: The project is listed at 50% and the exam is 10%, so the tag is project-heavy. The syllabus's own project line items add to 45% while the summary says 50%; both figures are stored and not reconciled. This syllabus's formal prerequisites are only CS 2110 or CS 2261, each with a minimum grade of C. The catalog popup also allows ECE 2020 and ECE 2035 together, each with a minimum grade of C. Peer star ratings can scale every group grade down. A plagiarism quiz must be passed before other work.

title: Advanced Operating Systems

prerequisites.expression: CS 3210 with a minimum grade of C

requirements_fulfilled: Distributed System & Software Design and Systems & Architecture Thread — Advanced Systems & Architecture (1 class in CS 4210 or CS 4220 or ECE 4100)
description: Operating system abstractions and their implementations, multi-threading, efficient inter-address communication, high-level synchronization, introduction to multi-processor and distributed operating systems, real-time systems.
skills_developed: Explain operating-system structures, multicore and multi-process systems, distributed operating systems, and datacenter systems.
Compare systems-software designs and their effect on real-world systems.
Implement advanced systems-software features and design scalable services for a single node or a distributed environment.
exam_structure: 1 midterm (20%) and 1 final (25%). Exams are open access to papers, proctored with Honorlock, and not cumulative. Based on lectures and required reading.
grading_breakdown: Programming assignments 50%, midterm 20%, final 25%, class participation 5%. Scale: A 90–100, B 80–89, C 70–79, D 60–69, F 0–59. No curve stated. A passing average is required in both the projects and the exams in order to pass.
assignment_load: Four programming projects. The first project is individual. After that, students either continue the assigned sequence or replace the remaining projects with an instructor-approved project. Strong C programming skills are stated as essential. No textbook; required reading is research papers.

has_lab.note: Syllabus describes projects, exams, and paper reading. No lab component is stated.

average_gpa.note: Aggregate across sections, not per instructor.

notable_features: Projects are 50% and exams are 45%, so the tag is balanced. Cross-listed and held jointly with CS 6210; undergraduates see the same content, with possible differences in exam and project evaluation. Catalog prerequisite remains CS 3210 with a minimum grade of C. One of three courses that can satisfy Advanced Systems & Architecture. Attendance is encouraged and not required.

title: Advanced Computer Organization

prerequisites.expression: ECE 3056 with a minimum grade of D or ECE 3057 with a minimum grade of D or ECE 3058 with a minimum grade of D

requirements_fulfilled: Distributed System & Software Design and Systems & Architecture Thread — Advanced Systems & Architecture (1 class in CS 4210 or CS 4220 or ECE 4100)
description: Modern computer architecture, including branch prediction, out-of-order execution, cache optimizations, multi-level caches, memory and storage, cache coherence and consistency, and multi- and many-core processors. The same syllabus covers CS 4290, ECE 4100, CS 6290, and ECE 6100. Catalog text: comprehensive coverage of architecture and system issues in high-performance workstation/PC design, with emphasis on quantitative evaluation. Credit is not allowed for both ECE 4100 and any of ECE 6100, CS 4290, or CS 6290.
skills_developed: Understand the design and operation of modern in-order and out-of-order processors.
Use benchmarking and simulation to choose design and parameters for key parts of the processor core.
Understand and model on-chip interconnects, cache coherence, and consistency models.
Make decisions about how processor hardware interacts with system and application software.
exam_structure: 1 midterm (20%) and 1 final (30%). The final includes questions on midterm material. No make-up exams unless the Dean of Students advises it.
grading_breakdown: Projects 50% and exams 50%. Project 0 is 5%, project 1 is 10%, project 2 is 15%, project 3 is 20%. Midterm 20%, final 30%. Planned letter cutoffs are A at 90% and above, B at 80% and above, and so on. A curve is possible: if that scale produces too few As, thresholds may be lowered or some sort of curve used. No required textbook.
assignment_load: Four projects, each larger than the previous one. Completed individually or in teams of two, as each assignment specifies. The syllabus allows partners only on projects 2 and 3.

has_lab.note: Syllabus describes projects and exams. No lab component is stated.

average_gpa.note: Aggregate across sections, not per instructor.

notable_features: Projects and exams are each 50%, so the tag is balanced. One syllabus covers the cross-listed set CS 4290 / ECE 4100 / CS 6290 / ECE 6100, all listed as 3 credits. Catalog attribute: TCES. Credit is not allowed for both ECE 4100 and any of ECE 6100, CS 4290, or CS 6290. Lecture attendance is not tracked and is not part of the grade. One of three courses that can satisfy Advanced Systems & Architecture.
